spatial_claims.claim: Third proportionals O and P are constructed as line segments satisfying AB:CD = CD:O and EF:GH = GH:P. No spatial position claim, only ratio relationship.

Similar and similarly situated figures KAB, LCD are in the duplicate ratio of corresponding sides AB, CD (invoking 6.19/6.20). This is a ratio fact about similar figures, not a spatial configuration claim.
Similarly, MF:NH = EF:P via duplicate ratio. Same ratio fact, no spatial claim.
Fourth proportional X constructed so AB:CD = EF:X, and third proportional Y so EF:X = X:Y. Auxiliary line segments defined by ratio, no spatial position.
Proof by contradiction using ratio inequalities (5.8, 5.10, 5.13) that X = GH. Entirely algebraic comparison of magnitudes.

configuration_map: All objects in the proof are line segments (AB, CD, EF, GH, O, P, X, Y) and similar rectilineal figures (KAB, LCD, MF, NH) described on those segments. No point is ever claimed to lie inside, outside, or on any figure. No ray ordering, betweenness, or angle decomposition appears. The auxiliary segments O, P, X, Y are defined purely through ratio relationships (third and fourth proportionals via 6.11 and 6.12). The entire argument proceeds through Book V proportion theory, using the geometric results 6.19 and 6.20 only as established ratio identities. There is no spatial configuration to track.
pass_reason: The proof is entirely ratio-theoretic, using Book V proportion theory (5.7-5.13, 5.22) and previously established results about duplicate ratios of similar figures (6.19, 6.20, D5.9). No spatial configuration claims are made: no point positions, no ray orderings, no angle decompositions, no inside/outside arguments. All auxiliary objects are line segments defined by ratio relationships. There are no spatial claims that could be mutually inconsistent.
